title: The Little Trucks Who Move the Moon | Calm Bedtime Story
description: Have you ever wondered how the Moon climbs into the sky each night? It's the little trucks! Every evening, five friendly trucks — Pip, Dot, Rosa, Mo and Nell — gently move the big round Moon up over the hills and set it softly among the stars, so it can shine on all the sleeping children. A slow, magical bedtime story for little ones who love trucks and the Moon. New Moon Trucks stories every week.
narration:
Have you ever wondered how the Moon gets up into the sky?

Well. I'll tell you a secret. It's the little trucks who move the Moon.

Every evening, when the sky turns soft and pink and the day grows sleepy, the big round Moon waits at the bottom of the hill. It is much too big to climb up by itself. So the five little trucks come to help.

First comes Dot, the careful yellow digger. Slowly, gently, she clears a smooth path through the soft moon dust, so the Moon can roll along without a single bump. There. All tidy.

Next comes Pip, the little blue dump truck, the smallest of them all, with the kindest eyes. He rolls right up beside the great round Moon and leans against it with his soft, round back.

Then comes Rosa, the cheerful pink loader, with her wide gentle scoop. She tucks it underneath the Moon to hold it steady and safe.

Then comes Mo, the round red mixer, humming his sleepy tune — hmmmm, hmmmm — a song to help everybody work together, slow and calm.

And last comes Nell, the tall green crane, slow and strong and gentle, reaching up high among the early stars.

"Ready?" whispered Pip.

"Ready," said all the trucks.

And softly, ever so softly, they began to move the Moon up the hill.

rrm… rrm… rrm…

Pip pushed. Rosa held it steady. Dot smoothed the way ahead. And Mo hummed his gentle tune. The Moon rolled forward just a little. Then a little more. The little trucks did not hurry. You can never hurry the Moon.

rrm… rrm… rrm…

Up, and up, and up the gentle hill they went, until at last they reached the very top, where the sky was wide and dark and waiting, and all the stars were twinkling, holding a place for the Moon.

Then tall Nell reached up with her long, long arm. Carefully, ever so carefully, she lifted the big round Moon up… up… up… and set it ever so softly onto its cushion of stars.

There.

The Moon settled into the sky with a happy little glow. And all at once, its soft white light spilled down over the whole wide world — over the hills, over the trees, over the rivers and the rooftops, over every sleepy little child tucked up warm in bed.

The five little trucks looked up at the Moon they had moved, glowing high and round and beautiful, and they felt very proud, and very, very sleepy.

Their job was done.

Slowly, they rolled back down the gentle hill to their cosy little shed. Dot yawned. Pip's eyes grew heavy. Rosa lowered her scoop. Mo's hum grew soft and slow. And tall Nell folded her long arm down to rest.

rrm… rrm… shhhhh.

And one by one, the little trucks who move the Moon curled up together, safe and snug, while the Moon they lifted kept watch over the sleeping world.

Goodnight, Dot. Goodnight, Pip. Goodnight, Rosa. Goodnight, Mo. Goodnight, tall quiet Nell.

Goodnight, big round Moon, shining softly in the sky.

And goodnight to you. Sleep now. The Moon is up. Everything is calm. Everything is well.
